calls.reason: The SPICE paper reports DALL-E 3 repeatedly failing to remove a violin bridge even after corrections in January 2025. This closely supports the stated limitation, although it does not verify the November deployment.

The original image sequences were not independently verified. Liu and colleagues demonstrate useful automated feedback in a different workflow, leaving ordinary ChatGPT part-specific correction unclear.

The linked annotations conflict with the success tally, and the comparison changes sampling and feedback procedures. The independent relations study tests different prompts and cannot establish the size of improvement here.

FineMatch finds weaknesses, while ConceptMix reports checking judgments close to human agreement. Neither tests the full corrective-feedback task, and the suggestion that new technology may be needed is hedged.

Conwell and GenAI-Bench document compositional failures, but GenAI-Bench also finds stronger basic-prompt performance. The broader characterization as superficial and offering little guarantee remains interpretive rhetoric.

Public Citizen documents corrupted labels and anatomy in an earlier Bing deployment, chiefly involving nonsense text. It does not establish incorrect label-to-part associations in November ChatGPT, whose bicycle images remain unverified.
